title: AnyLanguageModel 1.0 lets an Apple app swap the model without rewriting the session
friendlyTitle: A Swift update lets an Apple app change the model without a rewrite
summary: Hugging Face says AnyLanguageModel 1.0 is a drop-in stand-in for Apple's Foundation Models API. The same session code can call the system model, open-weight models through llama.cpp, MLX, or Core ML, or a hosted provider including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, and Hugging Face Inference Providers. Tool calling and guided generation work with every provider in this release. The post points to Gemma 4 E2B, about 3.4GB, and Liquid AI's LFM2.5 2.6B, about 1.7GB, as models that fit on an iPhone.
friendlySummary: Hugging Face says AnyLanguageModel 1.0 can stand in for Apple's built-in model API. The same session code can use Apple's system model, an open model on the device, or a hosted model from OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, or Hugging Face. In this release, tool use and structured replies work with every provider. The post points to two small models that fit on an iPhone: Google's Gemma 4 E2B, about 3.4GB, and Liquid AI's LFM2.5 2.6B, about 1.7GB.
whyItMatters: An app that started on Apple's on-device model can try a different local model, or a hosted one, without a second chat stack. The phone still has to have the memory. A 16GB MLX model is a Mac, not an iPhone. API keys are read from a closure, so a short-lived token from your own server is the intended pattern, not a key baked into the app.
